To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of goal-directed ontologies and a dialogue system that allows communication between humans and social robots, is a promising direction for the future development of human-robot interaction in service industry.
the dialogue model and the architecture of the dialogue system are crucial for the success of human-robot communication.

(1) goal-directed ontologies are suitable for modelling human-robot dialogues, (2) a dialogue model that uses a dialogue ontology and a dialogue manager can be used in a human-robot interaction scenario, and (3) a dialogue model can be used for explaining activities to a human user.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of dialogue systems that can enable robots to engage in human-robot interactions in service industries.
the development of a dialogue system based on a dialogue model that allows the user to interact with the robot in order to achieve the goal of the interaction.

dialogue systems that allow human-robot communication, in which a robot partner is able to understand and communicate with humans, and in which the robot partner can engage in dialogues that are related to tasks and activities of service robots in elder-care environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the paper presents a dialogue model that enables a human to communicate with a robot partner and engage the robot in interactions concerning tasks, activities, and the environment related to elder-care.
we are not ready to deploy robots into service industries, but we are ready to start developing the necessary technologies and methodologies to make this possible.
the dialogue system described in the paper is a promising approach for the development of social robots that can communicate and interact with humans, on topics related to service industries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for human-robot dialogues that enables the robot to communicate with people in service industries and to engage in conversations about tasks, activities and events.
the paper presents a dialogue model for human-robot interaction in service industries, based on a domain-specific ontology and on the goal-directed dialogue framework.
we have developed a framework for a dialogue system that is based on goal-directed ontology, and we have tested this dialogue framework in a real-life environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the robot should be able to communicate in a natural language, and to understand the meaning of the user’s utterances, in a way that is similar to how humans communicate with each other.
a dialogue system that is able to communicate in natural language with humans is a necessary component of an intelligent system that can support the activities of people in the service industry.
goal-directed models are suitable for dialogue management in human-robot interactions.
